ChatVerse 2.0 is a ground-up rebuild of the original scaffold into a research-grade, end-to-end
encrypted messaging platform. Every guarantee is written down in a protocol specification,
enforced by an index or a cryptographic primitive, covered by a test, and measured by a
benchmark whose results ship with this release.

## Highlights

- **One wire contract.** `@chatverse/protocol` defines the models, typed Socket.IO events with
  acknowledgements, REST contracts, shared zod schemas, stable error codes and a hybrid logical
  clock. The normative spec is `docs/PROTOCOL.md`.
- **Ordered, exactly-once visible delivery.** Dense per-conversation sequence numbers, client
  idempotency keys and a per-conversation ordered send section (in-process queue plus a Redis
  lock across nodes) give gap detection, resumable sync and in-order fan-out.
- **End-to-end encryption.** X3DH, Double Ratchet and Sender Keys on audited `@noble` primitives
  in `@chatverse/crypto`. Keys never leave the browser; the server stores public keys and
  ciphertext only.
- **Horizontal scaling.** Stateless API nodes coordinated through Redis for sequencing, presence,
  locks, rate limits and Socket.IO fan-out, optionally on a dedicated adapter Redis
  (`REDIS_ADAPTER_URL`).
- **Reproducible benchmarks.** A load generator that speaks the real protocol. Baselines are
  attached: 100 % delivery, zero duplicates and zero ordering violations in every run; median
  end-to-end latency of 2 ms at 4,000 deliveries/s on one node; zero loss across forced
  disconnects.
- **Tests at every layer.** 13 protocol, 23 crypto, 47 API and 26 web unit and integration
  tests, plus a Playwright suite that drives real browsers against the real server and crypto.

## Findings documented in `docs/EVALUATION.md`

The benchmark and browser suites found five issues during development, each fixed or recorded:
emission order differing from sequence order on one node and across two nodes, a harness
de-phasing bug, an interrupted-conversation-load bug on reconnect, and a concurrency bug in
client-side decryption that only appeared on slower machines. One proposed optimisation (batching
conversation bookkeeping writes) was measured, found to have no effect, and removed.

## Upgrading from 1.x

1.x never compiled and has no deployments to migrate. Start from `README.md` and
`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.
